NDT training in Arkansas: how it works for Arkansas employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT trains Arkansas technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A for Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory is delivered live online anywhere in the state, and hands-on practical training is delivered onsite at your employer's facility, whether that is a steel mill in the Delta, a refinery in south Arkansas or a fabrication shop in central Arkansas, under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice. Quotes on request.

This page covers the whole state rather than a single city, because that is how NDT work in Arkansas is distributed. The inspection market here is not concentrated in one metro. It is spread across the Mississippi County steel corridor around Blytheville and Osceola, the oil, chemical and brine country around El Dorado, Smackover and Magnolia, the defence plants of the Camden area, the nuclear and power stations along the Arkansas River valley, the aviation and manufacturing base of Little Rock, and the growing industrial and construction economy of northwest Arkansas. A technician in Jonesboro and one in Texarkana may be doing completely different jobs, and a training plan has to reflect that.

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Arkansas and does not claim one. We deliver the classroom portion live online, so a technician in Fort Smith or Pine Bluff can join without driving to Memphis, Dallas or Tulsa, and we bring practical training to your facility. Request an Arkansas training quote and we will reply with cohort and onsite options within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Arkansas

All courses are built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and are offered at Level I, Level II and as Level III examination preparation. The third column shows where Arkansas employers typically apply each method. It is market context; your employer's written practice and client specifications decide what you need.

MethodLevelsWhat Arkansas employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (Ultrasonic Testing)I, II, III prepPlate and slab inspection at steel mills, weld inspection at fabrication shops, thickness surveys on refinery and chemical-plant piping and vesselsLevel I: employer entry rules; Level II: Level I plus experience per written practice
PAUT (Phased Array UT)II, III prepWeld inspection on heavy fabrication and pressure equipment, corrosion mapping at refineries and brine-processing plantsUT Level II (or concurrent) recommended
TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction)II, III prepThick-section weld sizing on vessels and power-plant componentsUT Level II recommended
RT (Radiographic Testing)I, II, III prepPipeline and piping weld radiography, pressure-vessel fabrication, casting inspectionState radiation safety requirements apply separately; see below
MT (Magnetic Particle Testing)I, II, III prepStructural steel, mill equipment, cranes, rail and truck components, heavy fabrication weldsEmployer entry rules
PT (Liquid Penetrant Testing)I, II, III prepStainless piping, aerospace and defence components, valves and machined partsEmployer entry rules
VT (Visual Testing)I, II, III prepWeld visual inspection, tank and structural surveys, bridge and plant condition inspectionEmployer entry rules
ET (Eddy Current Testing)I, II, III prepAircraft structures and components, heat-exchanger and condenser tubing in power and chemical plantsEmployer entry rules

UT course content. Wave theory, transducer selection, couplants, calibration and reference standards, thickness gauging, angle-beam weld scanning, DAC and TCG, flaw evaluation and reporting. Because steel production is such a big part of the Arkansas market, we cover straight-beam inspection of plate and lamination detection, not just weld scanning.

PAUT and TOFD content. Focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scanning, scan plans and coverage, TOFD set-up and interpretation, and data analysis. These methods are increasingly written into specifications for pressure equipment and heavy fabrication in the region.

RT content. Source types, exposure geometry, film and digital radiography, image quality indicators, and weld and casting interpretation. The course covers the NDT technique; the radiation safety training and certification needed to use sources is a separate regulatory requirement.

MT, PT, VT and ET content. Method physics, equipment and consumables, technique selection, applicable acceptance criteria, and documentation. For Level III candidates we run structured preparation for the Basic, Method and Specific examinations; see ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Arkansas, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. There is no state NDT licence in Arkansas; the company that employs you certifies you against its written practice. The path is:

  1. Employer written practice. Defines training hours, experience hours, examinations and pass marks for each method and level.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the method-specific formal training required. Atlantis NDT delivers it live online or onsite. For recommended minimums, use our training-requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented, supervised experience in the method. Keep a signed log; if you move between a mill job and a plant job, record which is which.
  4. General examination on method theory.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, administered under a Level III.
  7. Vision examination, near-vision and colour contrast, usually annual.
  8. Employer certification, approved by the responsible Level III.
  9. Recertification at the interval in the written practice.

Our SNT-TC-1A certification guide explains each stage, including how certification transfers, or does not, when you change employer.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Arkansas crews

  • Live online. Real-time instructor-led classes with questions and quizzes. Ideal for a state where technicians are spread across small towns and long drives. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. We deliver practical training at your mill, plant or shop, using your equipment, procedures and representative specimens, under Level III oversight. Ask about onsite training for your Arkansas crew.
  • Dedicated cohorts when several candidates are ready at once.

Working around outages and turnarounds. Arkansas power stations schedule refuelling and maintenance outages, refineries and chemical plants run periodic turnarounds, and steel mills plan maintenance shutdowns. Those are the weeks your people are least available and most needed. We plan online theory in the quieter periods beforehand so your crew is ready, and schedule practical sessions outside outage windows. Tell us your plant calendar and we will work to it.

The practical exam is always performed on real specimens under Level III oversight, never online.

Where NDT technicians work in Arkansas

  • Steel in Mississippi County. Northeast Arkansas has become one of the largest steel-producing areas in the country, with Nucor operations around Blytheville and the Big River Steel mills at Osceola. Mills need UT for plate and products, MT and VT on equipment and cranes, and inspection support during maintenance outages. This is the single biggest reason Arkansas NDT demand has grown.
  • Oil, refining and chemicals in south Arkansas. El Dorado is home to a refinery and chemical operations, and the Smackover area has a long oil history. The bromine industry around Magnolia and El Dorado processes brine from the Smackover Formation, and several companies are now developing lithium extraction from that brine. Refinery and chemical work typically references API and ASME codes for in-service inspection, ASME B31.3 piping and ASME Section VIII vessels, with ASME Section V governing NDT technique.
  • Defence manufacturing around Camden. The Highland Industrial Park area hosts missile and rocket-motor manufacturing for major defence contractors. Defence and aerospace work often adds NAS 410 or military standards to personnel qualification; Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only, but the method knowledge carries across.
  • Power generation. Arkansas Nuclear One near Russellville is the state's nuclear station, and the state also has large coal and gas-fired plants. Power plants need UT, ET on condenser and heat-exchanger tubes, MT and PT during outages. Nuclear work has additional requirements set by the plant's own programme.
  • Aviation in Little Rock. Little Rock hosts business-jet completion and maintenance work, and Little Rock Air Force Base is home to C-130 operations and training. Aircraft NDT relies on ET, PT, UT and VT.
  • Pipelines and gas. Natural-gas production in the Fayetteville Shale of north-central Arkansas and interstate pipelines crossing the state generate weld inspection under API 1104 and integrity work.
  • Fabrication, rail and infrastructure. Fabrication shops across the state build tanks, vessels, structural steel and trailers; rail lines and river terminals on the Arkansas and Mississippi rivers, and ARDOT bridge programmes, need VT, MT and UT, often under AWS D1.1 or AWS D1.5 for bridges.

Radiography licensing in Arkansas. Arkansas is an NRC Agreement State, so the Arkansas Department of Health's radiation control programme, rather than the NRC, licenses the use of radioactive materials and radiation-producing machines within the state. Companies performing industrial radiography need the appropriate state licence or registration, and individual radiographers must hold the radiographer certification and radiation safety training the regulations require. Our RT course teaches technique and interpretation; it is not a substitute for that regulatory qualification. Confirm current requirements with the Arkansas Department of Health and your company's radiation safety officer, especially if you also work across the border in Texas, Louisiana or Oklahoma, where rules differ.

What Arkansas employers typically ask for. Mill and fabrication roles usually want SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT and MT, sometimes PT and VT. Refinery and chemical contractors frequently list UT, PAUT and VT and may also ask for API 510, 570 or 653 or AWS CWI for inspector roles. Atlantis does not train for those programmes. For earnings context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Arkansas NDT companies

Arkansas has many small and mid-sized NDT providers and in-house QC departments that do not employ a full-time Level III. SNT-TC-1A still requires a written practice and Level III responsibility for procedures and exams. We provide:

  • Written practices drafted or revised for your methods and clients. See NDT written practice development.
  • Procedures for UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT, PT, VT and RT technique aligned to the ASME, API or AWS documents your clients reference.
  • Level III examinations and certification records that stand up in a customer or registrar audit.
  • Corporate training plans for mill or plant QC teams. See corporate NDT training.

Book a Level III consultation, or read our SNT-TC-1A guidance first.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods across 5 environments: NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site, and storage tank. Arkansas fabrication technicians will get most from the welding workshop; refinery and brine-plant crews from the oil and gas and tank scenes; Little Rock aviation technicians from the hangar.

It is a practice tool only. It does not replace hands-on training with real instruments, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens under a Level III.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who designs the curriculum and oversees onsite programmes and examination content.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Arkansas

How do I get NDT certified in Arkansas?

Get hired or sponsored by an employer that certifies under SNT-TC-1A, complete the training and supervised experience its written practice requires, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Atlantis NDT provides the training and exam preparation.

Can I take NDT training online in Arkansas?

Yes. The classroom portion runs live online, so you can join from anywhere in the state. Practical training and the practical exam are completed hands-on at your employer's facility or an arranged location. See online NDT training.

Is there an NDT school in Little Rock or northwest Arkansas?

Atlantis NDT does not run a physical school in Arkansas. We train online and onsite at employers' facilities anywhere in the state.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom and experience minimums in your employer's written practice and whether you already hold Level I. Look up the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums in our training-requirements matrix; we then fit the classroom portion to your shift pattern.

Do I need a license for radiography in Arkansas?

Arkansas is an Agreement State, so radiation-source use is regulated by the Arkansas Department of Health. Your employer needs the appropriate licence or registration and radiographers need the certification and radiation safety training the state rules require. Check with the department and your radiation safety officer.

What does NDT training cost in Arkansas?

We do not publish prices. It depends on method, level, group size, and online or onsite delivery. Request a quote; cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Arkansas employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used personnel qualification basis among US industrial employers, including mills, refineries and fabrication shops in Arkansas. Certification is issued by, and belongs to, the employer.

Which NDT methods are most useful for the steel mills in northeast Arkansas?

UT and MT are the core methods for mill products and equipment, with VT and PT as common additions. Ask the mill or contractor which methods their inspection scopes use before choosing.

Can you train our plant crew before a nuclear or fossil outage?

Yes. We plan online theory ahead of the outage and practical sessions outside it. Nuclear sites have their own additional qualification requirements, which your plant programme defines.

Do you offer CWI or API inspector courses in Arkansas?

No. Atlantis NDT trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Those credentials are issued by AWS and API respectively.

How can I prepare for the practical exam?

Use the Practical NDT simulator to rehearse, then complete hands-on training on real specimens. The exam itself is always on real specimens under a Level III.

Where can I find UT Level 2 practice questions?

Try our UT Level 2 practice questions and the mock exams included in the course.
